finding: src/anomaly/search.py:166 matched_on deliberately discards genuine matches and collapses query scores.
rationale: The blocker is directly reachable: canonical signals can repeat a candidate value in both statement and preview, the gated code records every matching field but unconditionally keeps only the final one and derives query_score from that truncated list, while the locked acceptance and plan require matched_on details without defining this hidden field-order precedence.

evidence.output: Lines 146-150 assign matched_on = _matched_fields(fields, terms), expose it, and set query_score = len(matched_on); lines 159-170 append every matching field, but line 173 returns only matches[-1:].

_search_fields orders statement first and flattened preview fields last; _flatten_preview emits each preview leaf as its own public field, so matches[-1:] selects by producer order rather than an explicit relevance rule.

The signal-alpha fixture contains Acme in statement at line 39 and preview.vendor at line 42, while the Acme case at line 266 and assertion at lines 281-287 require only preview.vendor, thereby codifying the truncation.

The canonical producer spreads the detector result into the signal, builds preview from that same result, and builds statement with candidate_id; candidate_id can therefore genuinely occur in both searchable statement and preview on real produced signals.

evidence.output: Locked AC5 requires matched_on details. The plan defines matched_on as an ordered list of public-field match dictionaries and query_score as a retrieval-only value ordered descending, but states no most-specific-only or last-field precedence.
